step.name: Step 1
step.text: Planning a bathroom addition? This checklist will help you cover all your bases to ensure a smooth project!

step.name: Step 2
step.text: **Step 1: Define Your Vision and Layout.** Before anything else, clearly picture what you want. Think about the layout of your new bathroom and the fixtures you'd like to include. Will it be a half-bath or a full bath? Where will the toilet, sink, and shower/tub go? Having a clear idea here will guide all subsequent decisions.

step.name: Step 3
step.text: **Step 2: Confirm Plumbing, Electrical, and Mechanical Needs.** This is a big one. Does your desired layout require new plumbing lines, or can you tie into existing ones? What electrical outlets will you need, and where? Don't forget about ventilation! These details are crucial for both functionality and getting the necessary permits.

step.name: Step 4
step.text: **Step 3: Secure Required Permits.** Don't skip this! Depending on the scope of your addition, you'll likely need building, plumbing, and electrical permits. The review process can take a few weeks, so factor this into your timeline. A good contractor can often help you navigate this.

step.name: Step 5
step.text: **Step 4: Rough-In Work.** Once permits are in hand, the rough-in phase begins. This is where all the 'behind-the-walls' work happens—new framing, plumbing pipes, electrical wiring, and ductwork for ventilation. It's messy, but essential.

step.name: Step 6
step.text: **Step 5: Fixture and Finish Installation.** With the rough-in complete, it’s time for the fun part: installing your chosen toilet, sink, shower, and flooring. This is where your design vision really comes to life!

step.name: Step 7
step.text: **Step 6: Final Inspections and Handover.** Before you start enjoying your new space, final inspections will be done to ensure everything is up to code. Once approved, you're all set! Following these steps will help you create the bathroom you've always wanted. If you're unsure about any part of this process, especially with permits or complex plumbing, it's always smart to bring in a professional.
